therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Infusion of naturally-occurring regulatory T-cells to modulate immune response
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Ameliorate impaired immune recovery and address significant relapse incidence in haploidentical transplant setting
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with hematologic malignancies (AML, ALL, CML, MDS, NHL, CLL) undergoing haploidentical allogeneic transplant
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Maximum-tolerated dose (MTD) of regulatory and conventional T-cells

results.effect_size: Study terminated due to poor outcomes prior to sufficient accrual to set MTD
safety_signals: Acute graft vs host disease (3/7 patients)
results.dose_information: Only tested lowest dose level: T-reg 1x10e5/kg + T-con 1x10e5/kg, infused on days +14 and +16 respectively

context.investigator_commentary: Study was terminated due to poor outcomes prior to sufficient accrual to set the MTD. Median overall survival was only 3.7 months, with only 2 of 10 patients surviving at 1 year.
